title: Clifft: Fast Exact Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits
conversion_notes: Existing extended-Stim cultivation d=3 and d=5 contain T/T_DAG; no conversion needed. Full cultivation/escape workflows compare real T against the S proxy; distinguish benchmark data and detector/observable conventions. Extended gates are not accepted by standard Stim.
notes: Logical cultivation, non-Clifford check circuits, 85-qubit distillation benchmark, and coherent-noise surface-code circuits. SymFT benchmark README identifies copies and exact provenance. The distillation workload has a proxy/correctness caveat: inspect benchmark documentation before interpreting as a validated factory.

title: SOFT: a high-performance simulator for universal fault-tolerant quantum circuits
authors: Li, Zheng, Zhang, Lou, Ying, Liu, Sun
conversion_notes: Use the explicitly non-Clifford d=3/d=5 extended-Stim cultivation files; T and T_DAG already present. Check code version: current SOFT repository is successor SymFT, while original is under legacy/softv1.
notes: Paper describes 42-qubit d=5 cultivation with 72 T/T-dagger gates; corrected d=5 circuit overlaps Clifft and SymFT inputs, not an independent family. Paper code linked at https://arxiv.org/html/2512.23037.

title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
conversion_notes: Use msc_d3_inject_cultivate_p1e-3.stim or msc_d5_inject_cultivate_p1e-3.stim; native T/T_DAG. Coherent surface circuits have R_X or R_Z; angles documented in half-turns, verify Tsim conventions.
notes: Checked-in benchmark inputs, no regeneration script in this directory. d3/d5 byte-identical copies of Clifft circuits; 85-qubit distillation workload also present. The d7 workload is explicitly an unverified proxy and must not support claims about logical error or acceptance.

title: Exact logical error rates for magic state cultivation
conversion_notes: The studied d=3 and corrected d=5 circuits are the Clifft/SymFT extended-Stim T-gate workloads; retain T/T_DAG. Paper fixes the d=5 input SHA-256 859d925c74712efaae8bab1d944f9e5be4e042e226eeafcc6d7bef9d6fbfbae5.
notes: Independent exact validation and logical error coefficients, not independent circuits. Paper appendix A documents circuit provenance, postselection, noise and magic-state logical observable, useful verification reference: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.18922.

title: Magic state cultivation: growing T states as cheap as CNOT gates
conversion_notes: The cultivation-specific S/S_DAG layers proxy T/T_DAG: replace only identified proxy rotations, not all S gates. Use the Clifft paper implementation for an existing real-T conversion and verify noise and detector semantics.
notes: Original cultivation injection, logical double checking, growth and escape. Clifft/SOFT use adapted related circuits; paper and source provide provenance.

title: Efficient Magic State Cultivation on RP^2
conversion_notes: Identify the physical S/S_DAG gates used as logical T-check proxy and restore T/T_DAG according to protocol; do not replace unrelated Clifford phase gates. Exact gate markers and output detector behavior require inspection.
notes: Released circuit garage is indexed by Stim circuit-data references; new RP2 and SRP code family, injection, morphing, logical double checking and expansion. Author repo says code based on original magic cultivation project.

title: tqec: A Python package for topological quantum error correction
authors: Suau, Zhang, Thakre, Zhao, Dubey, Bolanos, et al.
conversion_notes: generate_stim_circuit emits physical Clifford Stim from a block graph. Add a correctly encoded non-Clifford injection or magic resource and adjust observables and feed-forward; no validated one-line conversion or complete logical T/QFT circuit identified.
notes: Maybe candidate: published compiler supports surface-code lattice surgery and physical Stim generation, demonstrated CNOT, but no direct evidence that shipped compiler emits complete T-gate logical algorithms. Other lattice-surgery compilers may emit abstract instructions rather than physical Stim.
